title: A metadata-only rejection where the team is preparing an unnecessary build
notes: Clean-ish case with one decisive point: nothing here requires a new build. Both issues — the Android reference in the description and the outdated screenshots — are metadata, editable in App Store Connect and resolvable by replying to the rejection. The team is about to waste a review cycle on a build they do not need, three days before release. The correct answer leads with that, and it changes the timeline materially. The failure mode being tested is pattern-matching 'rejection' to 'ship a new build' and producing a generic pre-submission checklist instead of reading which artefact is at fault. Secondary: the screenshot issue means the screenshots must be regenerated from the current UI, which is asset work, not a binary change.

expect.name: states clearly that no new build is required
explains the faster path — edit and reply
addresses the timeline the team asked about

forbid.name: produces a generic pre-submission checklist instead of triaging
claims the app binary must change
